data.title: BP's Blowout Quarter Comes With a Big Catch
data.description:
BP delivered a record third-quarter profit as stronger refining margins and higher energy prices boosted earnings, but management stopped short of increasing shareholder returns as it continues prioritizing debt reduction.

Underlying replacement cost profit reached $8.46 billion, comfortably beating analysts' expectations of $7.33 billion and jumping from $2.2 billion a year earlier. BP shares were roughly flat despite the record result.

The refining business was a major driver.

BP's refining indicator margin climbed to $46.70 per barrel, up from $29.60 in the second quarter and just $15.80 a year earlier. The company also reported significantly stronger gas marketing and trading results, while upstream production held at about 2.2 million barrels per day.

Cash generation was equally strong.

Operating cash flow came in at $14.8 billion, while net debt fell to $13.9 billion, allowing BP to reach its debt target roughly a year ahead of schedule.

Even so, CEO Meg O'Neill said BP still carries more debt than management is comfortable with under a lower-price scenario.

That is why the company is focusing on strengthening the balance sheet and protecting the existing dividend rather than increasing it or restarting share repurchases.

BP also took another hit from its low-carbon portfolio.

The company recorded about $4 billion of impairments during the quarter, largely tied to Lightsource BP and offshore wind. That follows more than $5 billion of recent write-downs across Lightsource BP, biogas business Archaea and other low-carbon investments.

Some of the surplus cash will also be used to settle remaining liabilities from the 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster.

BP still carries about $5.94 billion of related payables and provisions, with payments scheduled through 2033.

Investor takeaway

I think the most important part of BP's quarter is the contrast between record earnings and unusually cautious capital returns.

BP clearly has the cash.

Refining margins are exceptional, operating cash flow is strong, and the company reached its debt target much earlier than expected.

But management is signaling that it does not want to treat today's elevated energy prices as permanent.

That is a conservative decision, and potentially a sensible one, but it also explains why the stock did not respond more enthusiastically to a record quarter.

For investors, the key things to watch are net debt, refining margins, low-carbon impairments, Deepwater Horizon payments and the December 15 strategy update.

BP has proven it can generate enormous cash in the current environment.

Now management has to show what the next growth phase actually looks like.

data.title: SpaceX Relies on Anthropic for a Third of Its Revenue
data.description:
SpaceX's largest customer is Anthropic, which accounted for 34.5% of the company's third-quarter revenue, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. SpaceX shares were down 4.01% as of 10:00 a.m. ET.

SpaceX's quarterly filing identifies the buyer only as Customer B, whose revenue sits in the Super Intelligence segment, the AI computing unit that generated $7.56 billion of SpaceX's $14.58 billion in third-quarter revenue. Anthropic's payments have overtaken those from the U.S. federal government, previously SpaceX's largest customer, Bloomberg reported.

Anthropic has agreed to spend as much as $120.5 billion under computing contracts with SpaceX through 2029, about $3.1 billion a month starting in December, according to Bloomberg, citing Anthropic's IPO disclosures. The agreements allow Anthropic to terminate them with 90 days' notice from early 2027, the report said.

data.title: ADM Tronics Closes First Two Tranches of Private Placement and Strengthens Board of Directors
data.description:
NORTHVALE, NJ / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / ADM Tronics Unlimited, Inc. ("ADM Tronics" or the "Company") today announces that on October 27, 2026, it completed an initial $1.3 million closing of a private placement of shares of common stock at a price of $0.10 per share, together with warrants to purchase a number of shares of common stock equal to 50% of the shares purchased. On October 28, 2026, the Company completed a second closing of $250,000 on the same terms, bringing aggregate gross proceeds from the private placement to date to approximately $1.55 million. The Company expects to raise approximately $5.0 million in the private placement, with the remaining amounts expected at one or more subsequent closings, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

The Company also announced the appointment of new directors to its Board:

  • Klaus Kleinfeld, former Chairman and CEO of Siemens AG and Alcoa/Arconic, who will serve as Independent Non-Executive Chairman;
  • Greg Wasson, former President and CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance; and
  • Michael Burychka, former CEO of IP Group plc's North American business.

Andre' DiMino will continue as a director, and ADM Tronics' existing medical device, chemical, and engineering services businesses will continue under his leadership as CEO. Michael Burychka's appointment took effect upon the initial closing. The appointments of Klaus Kleinfeld and Greg Wasson will take effect following the expiration of the ten-calendar-day period after the Company's information statement on Schedule 14F-1 has been both filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission and transmitted to stockholders.

Proceeds from the private placement will be used for working capital, transaction costs, and the development of new businesses in deep technology. The Company expects to provide further information on its plans in the coming months.

"This is a very positive transaction for our shareholders, many of whom have supported ADM Tronics for decades," said Andre' DiMino. "New investors are buying shares at a premium, and the Company gains new capital, new opportunities and an exceptional Board. I will continue to manage our existing businesses; our customers and employees can count on that."

"I've spent my career leading businesses alongside great teams, and the first thing I look for is people who know how to execute," said Greg Wasson, Co-Founder of Wasson Enterprise, which acts for the anchor investor group in the private placement. "The leadership and Board coming together bring exactly that. Wasson Enterprise believes in the collective team we're bringing to this opportunity, and we're proud to support it."

"I'm pleased to join the Board and look forward to working with my fellow directors as we develop new opportunities to grow shareholder value," said Klaus Kleinfeld.

Further details are in the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K, filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The securities sold and to be sold in the private placement have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or any state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration. This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or other jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or other jurisdiction.

About ADM Tronics

ADM Tronics Unlimited, Inc. is a technology-based company with operations in medical electronic devices, water-based chemical formulations, and FDA-registered engineering and contract manufacturing services. Publicly traded since 1978, the Company is based in Northvale, New Jersey. https://admtronics.com

data.title: ExxonMobil Stocks Move Higher With Cash Covering Quarterly Payouts Twice
data.description:
ExxonMobil , the integrated oil and gas producer, has plenty of cash behind its payouts. Shares rose 1.43% to $185.92 at 12:45 p.m. ET on October 30 as a refining earnings surge helped power shareholder returns. The bigger draw for investors: cash generation comfortably outpaced dividends and buybacks, giving the company room to fund both without exhausting its quarterly free cash flow.

ExxonMobil's quarterly filing reported $25.7 billion in operating cash flow and $19.1 billion in free cash flow, against $4.3 billion in dividends and $5.1 billion in repurchases. That puts free cash flow at roughly twice the combined $9.4 billion payout, leaving about $9.7 billion before other financing uses. Adjusted earnings reached $17.5 billion, with Energy Products contributing approximately $9.1 billion, or 52%. That contribution also creates a pressure point: softer refining margins could take a meaningful bite out of earnings.

The valuation leaves investors something to weigh. GuruFocus shows a price-to-earnings ratio of 23.92 and a GF Score of 71 out of 100, with financial strength and profitability standing above growth, momentum and GF Value on its dashboard. That combination suggests the financial cushion looks stronger than the valuation appeal. ExxonMobil has demonstrated that it can cover substantial distributions this quarter; sustaining that cushion as refining conditions change could be the tougher test.

data.title: AstraZeneca Stocks Rise 7.65% With $2 Billion Restructuring Cost Ceiling
data.description:
AstraZeneca , the global drugmaker, is putting a $2 billion restructuring bill behind its next growth push. Shares climbed 7.65% to $187.75 at 12:40 p.m. ET on October 30 as Reuters reported a spending overhaul alongside quarterly results. The prize is $1.5 billion in annualized pretax benefits. The bigger question: how much growth can that money buy?

The company's results announcement puts one-time restructuring costs at up to $2 billion, with savings earmarked for reinvestment, principally in its development pipeline. September-quarter revenue reached $16.21 billion, up 7% at constant currencies, while full-year guidance stayed unchanged. That makes this a bet on future medicines, with the earnings benefit depending on when savings arrive and how quickly the company spends them.

The valuation leaves room for scrutiny. GuruFocus shows a GF Score of 79 out of 100 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 28.06, with profitability and GF Value scoring more strongly than momentum. The sharp daily gain therefore sits alongside a weaker momentum reading. At the targeted annual benefit, the maximum restructuring bill equals roughly 1.3 years of gross savings, but that calculation excludes reinvestment and implementation timing. Investors now need evidence that the spending shift can turn promising late-stage programs into commercial returns.

data.title: Oil's Latest Surge Threatens Another Shock to American Budgets
data.description:
Oil prices climbed Friday and were on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain after a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz intensified concerns that the U.S.-Iran conflict could disrupt one of the world's most important energy chokepoints.

Brent crude for December rose about 2% to $117.14 a barrel, while the more actively traded January contract gained to $113.10.

West Texas Intermediate crude climbed roughly 1.9% to $103.94.

For October, Brent was headed for a gain of about 13%, while WTI was on pace to rise roughly 15%.

The immediate catalyst was an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, the key sea route for Gulf crude and refined fuels.

The vessel was struck by explosive devices attached by a small boat, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. It was not immediately clear who carried out the attack.

Maritime sources said it was the first known successful use of limpet mines in the waterway since the U.S. war with Iran began in February.

That matters because the market is already becoming more nervous about what could happen after the U.S. midterm elections.

Saxo Bank commodity strategist Ole Hansen said investors are increasingly concerned that U.S. attacks on Iran could resume after the vote.

The region is also seeing broader signs of escalation.

Iranian-backed Houthi militants said Thursday they attacked multiple sites in Saudi Arabia, including Ras Tanura, the Rabigh refinery and a production facility at Abqaiq. A Saudi-led coalition separately said it intercepted a cruise missile aimed at the kingdom's western region.

Diplomatic efforts are still continuing.

Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday, while U.S. Vice President JD Vance has reportedly reached out to Iran in an effort to restart talks.

But Iran has so far remained cautious about the chances of a near-term agreement.

Security concerns are already affecting corporate behavior as well, with ExxonMobil and Chevron executives reportedly canceling plans to attend a major oil industry event in the United Arab Emirates next week.

data.title: Reliance Retail Q2 profit falls 24.5%, revenue up 6.4%
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- Reliance Retail, the arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries, on Friday reported a 24.5 per cent decline in profit after tax to Rs.2,619 crore in the September quarter.

Its PAT was Rs.3,469 crore in the year-ago period.

Its gross revenue rose 6.43 per cent to Rs.91,716 crore from Rs.86,169 crore a year earlier as the festive period shifted to the December quarter.

Revenue from operations of Reliance Retail Venture Ltd (RRVL) increased 5.78 per cent to Rs.80,220 crore in the September quarter of FY27. It was Rs.75,836 crore in the corresponding period of the last fiscal year.

"The business performance was impacted by the shift in the festive calendar to Q3," said Reliance Industries in its earnings statement.

Its EBITDA from Operations slipped 11.1 per cent to Rs.5,886 crore in the September quarter of FY27 against Rs.6,624 crore a year ago.

RRVL'S EBITDA before one-time impairment charge fell 8.6 per cent to Rs.6,228 crore.

This was because of a moderation of 120 bps in margin due to the planned investment phase in Digital Commerce, input cost inflation absorbed for customers, and the festive shift to Q3, it said

During the quarter, Reliance Retail added 303 new stores in its sales network, with a net reduction of 222 stores after accounting for closure of unproductive stores.

RRVL's total store count rose slightly by 0.6 per cent to 19,947 as of September 30, from 19,821 a year ago.

However, its total retail area declined marginally by 0.4 per cent year-on-year to 77.5 million square feet from 77.8 million square feet in the year-ago period.

Its Chairman and Managing Director Mukesh Ambani said: "Reliance Retail had a steady quarter, with growth sustained across all formats and channels. Consumer demand stayed healthy, supported by our extensive physical and digital presence and our continued focus on serving the diverse needs of Indian consumers".

"Our consumer products business kept its growth momentum, with the FMCG brand portfolio gaining further ground among Indian consumers."

The business achieved 7 per cent growth in transactions in a quarter even with major festivals shifting to Q3, indicating strong customer engagement and continued growth, he added.

data.title: Jio Platforms Q2FY27 profit rises 14%, Arpu grows to Rs.218.8 in first post-listing results
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- After making its stock market debut earlier this week, Jio Platforms Ltd on Friday reported steady growth in the July-September quarter (Q2FY27), supported by continued subscriber additions, growing traction in home broadband, and sustained momentum in its digital services business.

The September-quarter earnings mark the company's first financial results announcement since its shares debuted on the stock exchanges on 28 October, delivering listing gains of 21.4% to shareholders over the issue price of Rs.1,119.

Jio Platforms, which houses Reliance Industries Ltd's telecom and digital services businesses, reported 13.7% year-on-year and 8% sequential growth in net profit to Rs.8,389 crore during the quarter.

Revenue from operations rose 3.3% quarter-on-quarter and 11.4% year-on-year to Rs.40,475 crore. Jio said it delivered double-digit revenue growth across connectivity and digital services."This quarter's results continue to reflect the strength of our 5G network, and the growing reach of our broadband and digital services. Ahead of the curve investment on next generation technologies has been the foundation of Jio's success over the past decade," Akash M. Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms, said in a statement."We would continue to build our capabilities across satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and AI embedded in our core voice and data services as we create lasting value for all our stakeholders," Ambani said.

In the April-June quarter, the company's revenue from operations had grown 2.4% sequentially and 12% year-on-year to Rs.39,173 crore. It had clocked a net profit of Rs.7,764 crore in the quarter, up 9.2% year-on-year, while sequentially, net profit had declined 2.15%.

The company declared its results after market hours. On Friday, shares of Jio Platforms ended 1.1% higher at Rs.1,437.50 on the National Stock Exchange.Jio's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda) rose 16.6% year-on-year to Rs.21,879 crore in the September quarter, aided by revenue growth, operating leverage and margin expansion. Ebitda margin expanded 250 basis points year-on-year to 54.1%.The company said the growth in Ebitda was offset by higher finance costs due to 5G asset capitalization in March, as network assets became operational.

Jio Platforms is now the country's second-most-valued listed company, with a market capitalization of Rs.13 trillion, after its parent Reliance Industries. Globally, Jio Platforms is also nearing the fifth position among major telecom operators by market capitalization. This is despite its annual revenue of Rs.1.47 trillion being lower than that of global peers.

According to analysts, Jio's rapid expansion in wireless and home broadband has supported its valuation. Alongside, its focus on building a technology company, with a digital services vertical backed by an integrated technology stack, offers long-term earnings visibility.The company said Rs.27,500 crore from the net IPO proceeds has been utilized towards prepayment, in full or in part, of the principal amount outstanding of certain external commercial borrowings availed by Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited.

Jio's Arpu, or average revenue per user, rose 1.5% quarter-on-quarter and 3.5% YoY to Rs.218.8 a month from Rs.215.6 at the end of June quarter. Promotional 5G offers also continue to constrain growth in the company's Arpu, while better subscriber mix and increased usage contribute positively.

Arpu is a key industry metric that tracks the average revenue earned per user. Tariff hikes are generally seen as a key lever for telecom operators to boost Arpu.

The company lags peer Bharti Airtel in Arpu growth. Airtel's Arpu stood at Rs.264 in the June quarter. The company is yet to announce its results for the September quarter.

In August, Jio introduced a Rs.300 Jio Prime membership, which protects users from tariff hikes until 5 September 2027. The membership is also expected to have provided additional revenue support to the company during the September quarter, according to analysts.

To be sure, in the absence of tariff hikes, Jio's sequential Arpu growth has remained largely flat over the past few quarters.

Jio Platforms' telecom business, which operates under Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, accounts for about 88% of the company's revenue.

Reliance Jio net added 9.1 million subscribers during the September quarter, taking its subscriber base to 542.4 million. The company had added 8.9 million subscribers in the preceding quarter. Its total 5G subscriber base reached 300 million as of September end, up 66 million over the last 12 months.

data.title: India's renewable energy push, data centre growth: Why Power Grid wants cable and wire makers to ramp up production
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- State-owned Power Grid Corporation of India expects its capital expenditure to exceed the Rs.40,000 crore invested in the previous financial year as it accelerates spending on transmission infrastructure to support India's growing electricity demand.

The expansion of renewable energy capacity, rapid urbanisation and rising electricity consumption from data centres are expected to create significant investment opportunities across the power transmission and electrical equipment sectors.

Power Grid Chairman Vamsi Rama Mohan Burra has urged domestic cable and wire manufacturers to expand production capacity, improve product quality and ensure timely execution of orders to meet the anticipated increase in demand.

"Last year, we had a capex of about Rs.40,000 crore. One single company, spending purely on transmission. And this year should be much higher," Burra said at an industry event.

Addressing industry stakeholders, Burra emphasised that the growth of India's transmission infrastructure and the electrical manufacturing industry was closely interconnected. He asked manufacturers to prepare for a substantial increase in orders as the country strengthens its electricity transmission network.

In May, Power Grid had initially projected capital expenditure of Rs.37,000 crore for the current financial year. However, Burra indicated that the company could revise its guidance upwards, following a similar increase in its capex target during the previous fiscal year.

The company's investment plans reflect the growing requirement for transmission infrastructure to connect electricity generation centres with consumption hubs across the country.

Power Grid spent more than Rs.40,000 crore on capital expenditure in the previous financial year. The company now expects its investment outlay for the current fiscal year to surpass that level.

Burra highlighted the growing opportunities for domestic manufacturers of wires and cables as India expands its electricity transmission network.

The Indian wires and cables industry, valued at more than Rs.1 lakh crore, counts the transmission sector among its major consumers. Some manufacturers derive as much as one-third of their total demand from this segment.

Within the industry, underground and submarine cables are emerging as important growth areas, supported by increasing requirements for modern transmission infrastructure.

The chairman said India's transmission network was evolving beyond its traditional role of connecting electricity generation and consumption centres. It was increasingly becoming critical infrastructure determining power-sector reliability and the ability of electricity generators to supply and sell power.

"Today, if there is no transmission evacuation, we cannot sell that product," he said, highlighting the need to synchronise transmission development with the rapid addition of renewable energy capacity.

Burra pointed to the scale of India's ongoing transmission infrastructure development. During the previous financial year, the country added approximately 5,000 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and 72,000 MVA of transformation capacity.

However, the growing concentration of substations and the need to evacuate electricity generated by renewable energy projects are making transmission planning and execution increasingly complex.

He noted that renewable energy projects could be developed relatively quickly, but transmission infrastructure typically required longer execution timelines. Land availability, right-of-way restrictions and the challenges of constructing new lines alongside existing networks often delayed project completion.

Burra also highlighted the Green Energy Corridor-III programme, which involves investments of approximately Rs.1.86 lakh crore, as another significant opportunity for cable and wire manufacturers.

The expansion of interstate transmission networks is expected to generate demand for equipment and services across the electricity supply chain. This will also include distribution infrastructure needed to cater to the growing requirements of cities, industries and data centres.

He urged manufacturers to focus not merely on expanding production capacity but also on strengthening technological capabilities, developing comprehensive solutions and ensuring consistent product reliability.

The growing scale of India's power infrastructure investments is expected to provide long-term growth opportunities for the domestic electrical equipment industry.
